name: Pircel for WooCommerce
author: Pircel

sections.description:
Pircel is your all-in-one delivery management solution. Enhance your e-commerce experience and streamline order-delivery flow.

Configuration

  1. From the WordPress admin sidebar, navigate to Settings > Pircel.
  2. Fill the settings in the General tab as instructed by Pircel.

External Services

This plugin connects the store to Pircel’s own service. If the merchant turns on error reports, it also reports its errors to Sentry, and if Pircel sets up alerts, it emails Pircel through Mailgun.

Pircel API
The plugin is the store’s connection to Pircel, which prices delivery at checkout, books shipments with carriers and tracks them. It calls the API URL set in the plugin’s settings, over HTTPS only (plain HTTP is allowed to a local development host). It sends:
– When the store connects to Pircel: the store’s web address, the plugin version, and the WooCommerce REST API key the plugin creates for Pircel.
– At checkout, each time the delivery destination, the cart or the payment method changes: the destination’s country, region, city and postcode; the cart’s products (title, description, SKU, price, quantity, weight, dimensions, categories and customs codes); the cart’s totals; and the payment method. No name, street, phone, email or order note.
– When an order is placed or paid: the order’s id, the recipient’s name, street, phone and email, the customer’s order note, the details given for a Recipient Logistics delivery, the chosen shipping rate, the payment method, the order’s totals, and how the order was placed.
– After that: refunds and edits that change what the courier collects, and requests for each shipment’s status and tracking numbers.
– When WooCommerce erases an order’s personal data: a request to erase that order’s shipment data, with the customer’s email and phone.

Pircel: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy

Sentry error reporting
Off by default. Only when the merchant turns on “Send Error Reports” in the plugin’s settings does the plugin report, on a production site, its own errors and checkouts where it could not show or price shipping rates to Sentry, which Pircel uses to find and fix faults. A report holds only:
– The error message and stack trace, with file paths inside the WordPress install.
– The plugin, WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP versions, the server’s operating system, the store’s currency, tax and shipping settings and active payment methods, and the shop’s name or a tag Pircel sets.
– The page’s address without its query string, and what kind of request it was (method, AJAX, cron, cart or checkout page).
– For an order: its id, status, totals, currency, payment and shipping method, how it was created and its item count.
– For a shipment: its id, carrier, service, status and cost.
– For a checkout without rates: the cart’s total and item count, the destination country, the payment method, the theme and shipping-related plugins, and how the rates section looked on the page.

A report never holds an IP address, browser user agent, request headers, query string, referrer, form field, user or customer id, or anyone’s name, address, email or phone.

Sentry is provided by Functional Software, Inc.: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy

Mailgun alert emails
Off unless Pircel sets up alerts in the plugin’s operations settings or in wp-config.php. The plugin then emails Pircel through Mailgun’s API when an order’s shipment is stuck, missing or could not be created. The email holds the order’s id, status and dates, the reason, and the order’s diagnostics, which include its billing and shipping addresses and contact details.

Mailgun is provided by Mailgun Technologies, Inc.: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy

Additional Information

For any questions and support, please e-mail us at info@pircel.com
sections.installation:
1. Unzip the plugin zip file.
  2. Upload the folder pircel to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  3. In the WordPress admin dashboard, go to Plugins and activate the Pircel plugin.
sections.faq:
How do I configure Pircel?

After activating the plugin, head over to the Pircel settings in your WordPress dashboard (Setting > Pircel).

Can I integrate Pircel with my existing e-commerce site?

Yes, if your site runs WooCommerce, you can seamlessly integrate Pircel.

Do digital products get charged shipping?

No. A product marked Virtual in WooCommerce is never quoted, never added to a parcel, and never
carries a delivery charge. An order containing only virtual products gets no shipping rates at all.

A product that is Downloadable but not Virtual — a printed book bundled with its PDF, say — still
ships normally. Downloadable on its own never stops something being delivered.

In a mixed basket, only the physical items decide the parcel’s weight and dimensions. The digital
lines still count toward the order total and anything collected on delivery, because the buyer owes
that money either way; they simply do not affect what the courier is asked to carry.

How does Pircel classify my products?

Pircel reports what each item is — a physical good, a digital good, a gift card or a service —
alongside whether it needs delivery. It reads this from the product type first: a gift card sold
through a gift-card plugin is reported as a gift card whether you post it or email it, and a
WooCommerce Bookings product is reported as a service.

Anything that needs delivery is reported as a physical good, whatever else comes with it — boxed
software with a licence key is still a physical good. For products that need no delivery, Pircel
looks for a marker left by a licence-key plugin, then falls back to the Downloadable checkbox.

Marker detection is best effort and covers specific plugins by name: License Manager for
WooCommerce and Digital License Manager. If you use a different one, your products will come
through unclassified until you add the filter shown below — that is expected, not a fault.

One case cannot be told apart from any of that: a product that is Virtual with no file attached and
no plugin marker might be an emailed activation key, a membership, or a booked session, and
WooCommerce records all three identically. Pircel reports those as unclassified rather than
guessing. This affects reporting only — such products are never charged shipping regardless.

If your store sells something Pircel classifies as unclassified, you can tell it what the product
is. Use the first filter if your plugin registers its own product type, the second if it marks
ordinary products with a custom field:

add_filter( 'pircel_product_type_kinds', function ( $kinds ) {
    $kinds['your-product-type'] = 'DIGITAL_GOOD';
    return $kinds;
} );

add_filter( 'pircel_product_meta_kinds', function ( $kinds ) {
    $kinds['your_custom_field'] = 'DIGITAL_GOOD';
    return $kinds;
} );

Accepted values are PHYSICAL_GOOD, DIGITAL_GOOD, SERVICE, GIFT_CARD and OTHER.
